The `:1907` literal is the real per-render rollup published to the bus (not a fallback) — built from `rollupProject(dockRows)` at line 1904, then destructured into the emit. I added `alive: rollupAlive` sourced from that same `rollup` object (no hand-computation), and added it to the effect's dependency array too: without that, a shell opening/closing could leave `alive` stale in the chrome — `worst`/`live`/`waiting` can all stay unchanged while only `alive` moves, which is precisely the staleness the ceiling split was fixing.

Checks: ① `dashboard && npx tsc --noEmit` — zero errors anywhere, including `WindowChrome.tsx`. ② `agent-status-project-rollup.test.ts` — 11/11 green. ③ `git status --porcelain` on my files — only `AgentSurface.tsx` modified plus my three untracked files, nothing else.
